name_note: Many genomes that GTDB places in the genus Bulleidia carry the NCBI label Solobacterium; the statements here are taken only from sources that name Bulleidia.

sentences.text: Bulleidia extructa has been described as a rarely recognized anaerobic Gram-positive bacterium with an oral and gastroenterological ecological niche that is difficult to isolate because it grows slowly in culture.

It has been reported that Bulleidia extructa is most often isolated from infections related to the oral cavity, including gingivitis and periodontitis, and has also been recovered from prosthetic hip joint infections.
A Bulleidia extructa strain from the periodontal pocket of a patient with periodontitis was reported to have an unusually compact genome of 1.38 Mb and a strongly reduced metabolic repertoire.
Phylogenomic analysis of that strain placed it within the Erysipelotrichales and showed close relatedness of Bulleidia to Solobacterium and Lactimicrobium.
Bulleidia is also found in the human intestine: a complete genome was reported for Bulleidia sp. 10714-15, an obligately anaerobic bacterium isolated from stool samples of colon cancer patients.
